messages.body_plain:
Well, either you read in the files as character vectors with scan and
use gsub on them (e.g., with a loop), or, if they all look like this,
...

# create factors
set.seed(1)

lev<-c(1:9, LETTERS[1:13])
f1<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))
f2<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))
f3<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))

# create two identical data frames with these factors
df<-df2<-data.frame(f1,f2,f3)

# look at the data frame df
lapply(df, table)
df

... then you can use the same logic as in my last response:

# recode the factors in df2
for (i in seq(df)) {
   levels(df2[,i])[levels(df2[,i]) %in%
LETTERS]<-match(levels(df2[,i])[which(levels(df2[,i]) %in% LETTERS)],
LETTERS)+9
}

# look at the result
lapply(df2, table) # done
df2 # done
table(df[,1], df2[,1]) # done

Without a concrete example of what the data look like, it's hard to
write something that will cover all possibilities, though.

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: saving vectors
messages.body_plain:
Hi

You have to write

cat("names", file=choose.files(), sep="\n") # cat("names",
choose.files(), sep="\n")

Otherwise, R thinks the string resulting from choose.files() is
another string to be printed, as in

cat(1:3, 4:6, sep="\n")

That is, it lets you select a file name and prints it out. If you use
the above, R knows that the string resulting from choose.files() is
meant to be cat's file argument.

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries

cat(names, file="C:\\_qclwr\\_outputfiles\\03-2-4_vector-a.txt", sep="\n")

posting work fine. In Stefan's 4/19 6:11 post, the script was written
as:

>cat("names", file=choose.files(), sep="\n") # cat("names",
>choose.files(), sep="\n")

so I wasn't writing the script:

>cat(some.char.vector, file=choose.files(), sep="\n")

which works,
but rather:

cat("some.char.vector", file=choose.files(), sep="\n")

which simply prints the vector name to a file.
